names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Σολόχων, Παμφαμήρ και Παμφυλών», with the rank word left off; the life page carries «Αγιος Παμφυλων» as its own head name and adds two further forms, «ή Παμφαλών ή Παμφαλιών».

Read out of the body of the Охридски пролог's second entry for 17. мај ст. ст., „То исто учинише и два његова друга: Памфамир и Памфалон“; свети, which the next sentence puts before it, is not a rank. **It is a different form of the name from the one this folder is named for** — Памфалон against the Greek «Παμφυλών» — and it is the very variant this folder's life already records saint.gr as giving, „also written Pamphalon or Pamphalion“. Stored exactly as the Prologue prints it. Measured before drafting with `foldchk.py`: no folder in the corpus holds this form in any language, and the only neighbouring fold in the gate's rows is `? "памфил" — pamphilus-of-caesarea, pamphilus-the-martyr`, which this form does not join.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Σολόχων, Παμφαμήρ και Παμφυλών»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives him as one of three head names on one page — hence three folders. **The display name takes the day line's form** and the two variants the body offers, Πamphalon and Pamphalion, are recorded in the life and in the `names` note rather than added as separate forms, the page giving no ground to prefer one. **He is not one of the corpus's Pamphili**, which the namesweep raised, and which are other men on other days. **No year, so no `dates` object**, and no `locations` although Egypt and Chalcedon are named. No hymn is printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.05.2026 (17. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Солохон.“ — „То исто учинише и два његова друга: Памфамир и Памфалон … под којима издахнуше свети Памфамир и Памфалон.“

attestations.note: **A ROW OWED OUT OF A COMPANION'S HEADING**, on the same ground as Pamphamer's: the entry is headed for Solochon and the body narrates this man's martyrdom, which is the test that owes a row. Same menologion 17/5 the Greek row already carries. **THE SPELLING IS A THIRD FORM OF THIS NAME AND IT IS THE ONE THIS FOLDER'S LIFE ALREADY PREDICTED.** That life opens „the last name also written Pamphalon or Pamphalion“, off saint.gr; the Prologue writes **Памфалон**, which is that second form, against the Greek «Παμφυλών» this folder is named for. **The `sr` form stored is Памфалон, as printed, and the folder's `display_name` and slug are not touched** — a copied script form is never corrected towards another language's, and the display name is a settled English choice. **A YEAR READ AND DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN**, exactly as on Pamphamer: the 298 is Solochon's, given in the sentence after his revival, and the Prologue gives these two no year, so `dates` is untouched and this folder stays `undated`. **New here**: that he declared himself a Christian when the order came that all soldiers sacrifice, and that the officer was a commander and not a tribune. `types` untouched. No `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
